editorial:
You meet eight-year-old Peter, a quiet kid who hears tapping inside his bedroom wall while his parents insist it is only in his head. That simple setup pulls you into a tense home where every smile feels a little off, and every secret seems to hide behind closed doors. The movie keeps you guessing about who is telling the truth, mixing childhood fear with family drama in a way that feels personal and unsettling without going overboard.

The acting helps a lot, especially the parents, who can seem caring one minute and cold the next. The pacing stays steady, with small scares building toward bigger reveals, though some twists may feel familiar if you watch a lot of horror. It is best for viewers who like slow-burn tension, creepy houses, and stories about trust.
endingExplained: Peter finally breaks through the wall and finds Sarah, who says their parents locked her away. She convinces him to poison them, and he does. Once the parents are dead, Sarah comes out and shows her true, dangerous nature. She attacks Peter and Miss Devine, but Peter fights back and stops her. The final moments leave you with the idea that the real threat was never just in his imagination.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves creepy family horror and slow-burn tension.
